text:
ben: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak the hosted streaming path shows a 5-8% tail latency increase on p95/p99 for short chats (<150 tokens). Not huge but consistent across zones.

maya: ugh. saw any correlation with batch sizing or KV cache hit rate?

ben: Quick diff shows kernel selector now prefers the 'micro' kernel for sequences <32 because of a new latency model. That caused more fragmentation at ingress framing which increases syscall/writev pressure. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~2% for those flows.

noah: Can you paste the flame slice you saw?

ben: attaching a short sample (from canary region):
```
flame: ingress::parse_frame -> host::tokenize (18%) -> host::writev_coalesce (12%) -> kernel_selector::choose_micro (9%)
syscalls: writev spikes aligned with smallframe count + grpc windows
KV: kvcache_hits: 0.88 -> 0.86 after change
```

iris: That writev/coalesce number looks familiar — we've seen smallwrite churn before when proto framing doesn't coalesce. Did the selector change influence preparse path (e.g., early-unpack heuristics)?

ben: Yes — selector now signals `prefer_low_alloc` to preparse which disables some coalescing in the proxy shim for micro-kernel flows. So two things: different kernel choice and a side-effect flag that weakens ingress coalescing.

sam: low alloc wins on long sequences but for short chats it backfires. What's the % of short-chat traffic?

maya: ~42% of requests are <150 tokens during peak for the chat product. That matches the latency signal.

noah: Repro steps? I can run a local micro-bench to validate.

ben: repro script I used:
```bash
# replay short chat trace at 200rps against canary
./bench/replay_trace --trace traces/short_chat_150.json --rate 200 --target canary-host:8080
pprof: go tool pprof -http=:6060 /tmp/profiles/ingest.pb
```

ben: Observed 6% p99 tail worsening and ~12% increase in writev syscall count per second vs baseline.

iris: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert the flag that disables coalesce for micro-kernel; 2) adjust kernel selector thresholds to favor 'small-batch' kernel only for <16 tokens; 3) add a preparse coalesce override that forces coalesce when frame_count > 1.

sam: Which is fastest to ship?

maya: Reverting the preparse coalesce change is a one-line flip and safe for canary. Re-tuning thresholds will need model recompute and perf runs.

noah: I'm +1 on revert to confirm causality. We should also add metrics so we don't regress blind next time: ingress_frame_coalesce_ratio, selector_choice_by_len, smallwrite_syscalls/sec.

ben: filed a revert PR for the preparse flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621 — includes canary rollout plan.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/canary -> v2026.03.14-rc5 (pr/4621) by sam. ETA 10m. :rocket:

maya: also adding a perf test in the perf-harness to replay short_chat_150 at 200rps as a regression gate. I'll open a follow-up PR.

perf-bot: regression test added: perf/short-chat-150 (200rps) — baseline recorded.

noah: I'll run the local bench and verify after canary lands. If revert fixes it we'll keep revert and do a measured rework for selector weights later.

ben: After revert landed in canary we saw p99 back to baseline within 6 minutes. writev syscall rate returned to previous levels. KV hit-rate recovered.

isa: (joining late) any long-term follow-ups?

maya: yes — action items:
- (maya) add ingress_frame_coalesce_ratio metric + alert if < 0.7 for short flows
- (noah) run selector sensitivity sweep and propose new thresholds with perf numbers
- (iris) design a canary test that includes kv-shard-imbalance scenarios so selector changes don't mask cache effects
- (ben) document the preparse flag side-effects in the kernel-selector README

ben: created GH issues: runtime#1998 (metrics), runtime#1999 (selector-sweep), runtime#2000 (canary-eval).

sam: thanks everyone. Good catch — we avoided a subtle perf regression. Closing triage unless new signal appears. :thumbsup:
